questions.cardText:
[Medical Sciences] In toxicology, what is the concept of hormesis?
A. A small dose of a harmful substance can have beneficial effects
B. The toxicity of a substance differs for different individuals
C. Benefits of a substance are proportional to dosage
Answer: A.
questions.de: Wie heißt in der Toxikologie das Phänomen, dass eine kleine Dosis eines schädlichen Stoffes eine nützliche Wirkung hat?
questions.en: In toxicology, what is the name of the phenomenon in which a small dose of a harmful substance has a beneficial effect?

timeline.labelEn: Chester M. Southam and J. Ehrlich coin the term “hormesis” in the journal Phytopathology
timeline.labelDe: Chester M. Southam und J. Ehrlich prägen in der Zeitschrift Phytopathology den Begriff „Hormesis“

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following is a reason why bees buzz?
A. To slow down
B. To fly faster
C. To help with pollination
Answer: C. Bees buzz by rapidly vibrating their flight muscles. This buzzing helps them dislodge pollen from flowers, a process known as “buzz pollination.” However, some bees such as honey bees are not capable of buzz pollination.
questions.de: Wie heißt die Technik, bei der Bienen ihre Flugmuskeln schnell vibrieren lassen, um Pollen aus den Staubbeuteln einer Blüte zu schütteln?
questions.en: What is the name of the technique in which bees rapidly vibrate their flight muscles to shake pollen loose from a flower's anthers?

timeline.labelEn: Stephen Buchmann publishes his study of bees using vibration to collect pollen
timeline.labelDe: Stephen Buchmann veröffentlicht seine Studie über Bienen, die Pollen mit Vibration sammeln

questions.notes: Also called sonication. The card's “reason why bees buzz” is loose: bees also buzz simply from flying; buzz pollination is a specific use of the vibration. Wikipedia confirms honeybees cannot buzz-pollinate.
